description: Train a neural network to approximate the conformal map f: D -> Omega for parameterized domains Omega, then use the differentiable surrogate to optimize the Bloch radius via gradient descent. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) can enforce the Cauchy-Riemann equations as soft constraints. This provides a modern machine learning approach to an old analysis problem.
mathematical_formalization: Train NN f_theta: D -> C to minimize L = ||partial_{z_bar} f_theta||^2 + lambda * boundary_loss(f_theta, partial Omega). Then optimize B(Omega) = sup_z |f'_theta(z)|(1-|z|^2)/2 over domain parameters. Gradient: nabla_Omega B ~ nabla_theta B * (partial theta / partial Omega).
analogical_connections: Neural surrogate for conformal map ~ neural operator for PDE solutions (DeepONet, FNO)
PINN for Cauchy-Riemann ~ physics-informed loss in fluid dynamics
Domain parameterization ~ latent space in generative models
Gradient-based shape optimization ~ neural architecture search
implementation_hypothesis: Use a complex-valued neural network with holomorphic activation functions (or split real/imaginary parts). Train on boundary conditions for specific domains. Use automatic differentiation to compute f'(z) and the Bloch radius. Parameterize domain boundaries using B-splines and optimize the spline control points via backpropagation through the neural conformal map.
experiment_seed: Train a PINN to learn the conformal map from D to the strip. Verify that it recovers the known map. Then parameterize domains as disks with B-spline perturbations. Train the PINN for each domain, compute B_f, and use Adam optimizer on domain parameters. Compare with classical results.
